title: How to Clean a Steering Wheel (Leather, Alcantara, Plastic)
meta_description: How to clean a steering wheel safely: the right cleaner for leather, Alcantara and plastic, what not to use, and how to tell grime from wear.
excerpt: A shiny steering wheel isn't polished, it's grimy. Here's how to clean leather, Alcantara and plastic wheels safely, and what to keep well away from them.

hero.alt: BMW steering wheel rim covered in cleaning foam during an interior clean, with the instrument cluster behind

faq.q: What is the best way to clean a leather steering wheel?
faq.a: Spray a pH-neutral leather or interior cleaner onto a soft brush, work it into the rim a section at a time, then wipe it off with a clean microfibre and dry it.

faq.q: Why is my steering wheel shiny?
faq.a: On most modern leather wheels, shine is a build-up of skin oils and grime rather than polish. Clean leather usually has a soft, satin look.

faq.q: Can I use baby wipes or household wipes on my steering wheel?
faq.a: It's best not to. Many contain alcohol or degreasers that dry out and dull the leather's coating over time, and they leave a residue.

faq.q: How do you clean an Alcantara steering wheel?
faq.a: Use a cleaner made for Alcantara with very little moisture and a soft brush, blot it and let it dry. Then brush the fibres gently in one direction to lift them.

Is your steering wheel shiny? On most modern leather wheels that isn't polish. It's a build-up of skin oils, hand cream and grime, and it makes the rim less grippy.

The fix is gentle: a pH-neutral cleaner sprayed onto a soft brush, not onto the wheel, worked in a section at a time and wiped off with a clean microfibre. Household wipes, magic sponges and shiny dressings do more harm than good.

Our new guide covers leather, Alcantara and plastic wheels, what not to use, and how to tell grime from wear.
